items.content: When President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” you’d be forgiven for being skeptical that it would catch on. While most of the broader population is sticking with AI, some of Silicon Valley’s most powerful are falling in line and trying to give Trump the great AI rebrand he so desires.That Elon Musk was quick to jump on board, promising to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, isn’t surprising. When, hours after Donald Trump declared that “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!” Marc Benioff announced that Salesforce would rename AIForce to SIForce; it seemed like a quick capitulation, but not entirely out of character.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the summit where the executive order requiring government agencies to use the term “super intelligence” was announced. He’s also aligned himself with Trump, saying he believes the danger posed by AI is overblown. So it was somewhat predictable that when Nvidia declared that it would “commit” $1 billion to scientific advancement, that included “super intelligence research.” Of course, Huang has a lot to lose if he gets on Trump’s bad side.The latest to cave is Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, who attended the same AI summit as Huang along with Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai, Jeff Bezos, Dario Amodei, and Musk. In a post calling for building an “emergency brake” for AI yesterday, Nadella repeatedly referred to the technology as “super intelligence.”During Trump’s second term, Silicon Valley has repeatedly tried to ingratiate itself with the administration, after having a much more contentious relationship during his first term.

items.titleZh: 硅谷与特朗普改写人工智能的企图保持一致
items.descriptionZh:
报道称，特朗普政府正推动把“人工智能”（AI）改称为“超级智能”（Super Intelligence），并试图让这一新术语进入官方话语。文章描述，特朗普不仅宣布要重塑AI的名称，还宣称白宫会把继续使用“人工智能”一词的人视为“敌人”，并签署行政命令要求政府机构采用“超级智能”这一所谓“更准确”的表述。尽管公众仍普遍使用AI，但硅谷部分最有影响力的高管正在配合这一改名运动。

背景是，特朗普第二任期内，硅谷与政府的关系明显转向。经历了第一任期的紧张和对抗后，科技公司和高管频繁向政府靠拢，希望在监管、采购、补贴和政策环境中获得有利位置。因此，当特朗普推动AI改名时，一些科技领袖迅速跟进，把这当作政治站队和公关表态。

具体案例包括：马斯克迅速响应，承诺把“SpaceXAI”改名为“SpaceXSI”；Salesforce的马克·贝尼奥夫宣布将“AIForce”改为“SIForce”，被文章视为快速妥协。英伟达CEO黄仁勋出席了宣布相关行政命令的峰会，并曾表示AI带来的危险被夸大；英伟达随后宣布向科学进步“承诺”10亿美元，其中包含“超级智能研究”。文章指出，如果黄仁勋得罪特朗普，英伟达可能面临很大利益风险。最新跟进的是微软CEO萨提亚·纳德拉。他与黄仁勋、扎克伯格、皮查伊、贝索斯、Dario Amodei和马斯克等参加了同一场AI峰会，并在呼吁为AI建立“紧急刹车”的帖子中多次把该技术称为“超级智能”。

从技术角度看，这篇文章并没有发布新的芯片、模型或算法，也没有给出性能参数或对比数据；“超级智能”也不是一个已被实现的技术里程碑。通常，AI是更宽泛的术语，而“超级智能”指在几乎所有认知任务上超越人类水平的智能系统，目前仍属理论或远期概念。因此，把现有AI技术、治理和政策讨论统一改称“超级智能”，更像是一种话语重构和政治表态，可能夸大当前技术能力，并影响公众认知、监管框架、投资叙事以及政府项目命名。对AI芯片和算力行业而言，文中唯一可量化的动作是英伟达的10亿美元科学投入承诺；更广泛的影响则在于，政策术语变化可能牵动政府AI项目、研发资金、采购和监管沟通，但算力需求本身仍主要由模型规模、训练和推理部署等实际因素驱动。

items.title: Russia's Yandex bot traffic nearly eliminated overnight after Ukraine drone strikes cripple multiple of 'Russia's Google' data centers
items.description: Russian bot traffic falls dramatically as Ukraine takes out several Yandex data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Russian bot traffic has dropped dramatically in the past few days after Ukraine knocked out Yandex’s biggest data centers, with a third attack happening last night. Cloudflare reports that bot traffic from the Yandex network has dropped to just 0.4% of the maximum number of HTTP requests recorded in the past two weeks. It initially dropped to around 57% on Oct. 8, which happened when Ukraine hit a Yandex data center housing two supercomputers in Sasovo, Russia, located around 195 miles to the southeast of the Kremlin. A second, bigger Yandex campus in Kaluga, about 220 miles to the west of Sasovo, was knocked offline yesterday. These attacks are apparently Ukraine’s response to Moscow’s strikes on its own data centers, some of which resulted in the outage of some of the most popular piracy websites. (Image credit: CloudFlare)Yandex is Russia’s equivalent to Google, and its Yandex Cloud service status reports that at least 84 services are currently offline. Global internet monitoring firm NetBlocks said that Yandex’s network traffic has dropped to just 30% for Yandex Cloud and 63% for Yandex LLC, most likely resulting in slower internet services or complete disruption for the average Russian. Unfortunately, the ordinary Russian wouldn’t be able to use high-speed satellite internet as a backup, as Starlink does not work in Russia, while the competing Rassvet constellation has had a good number of its existing satellites fall back to the surface after launch.⚠️ Confirmed: Metrics show a second collapse in the networks of Russian tech giant Yandex after a new Ukrainian drone attack on data centers in Vladimir this morning. The campaign comes not long after Russia's threat to give Ukraine a "digital detox." https://t.co/jOVL5BjYNROctober 11, 2026These incidents are a result of the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, which escalated dramatically in 2022 after Russia’s failed attempt to capture Kyiv. However, many observers say that the war actually started in 2014 when Russian forces seized Crimea and occupied parts of eastern Ukraine after the fall of the pro-Russian government that year.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The hostilities, which have dragged on for years, saw the introduction of new technologies and strategies, specifically in drone warfare. It began with the wide deployment of commercially available drones on the front lines, typically for reconnaissance, dropping explosives, and kamikaze-style attacks. However, it has since evolved into long-range warfare, with specially built drones able to reach distances of over 1,500 miles and destroy Tu-95 strategic bombers situated well behind the front lines.The drone strikes on data centers are relatively new developments. While data centers on bases are often considered valid targets, Russia’s justification for the attacks on civilian data centers was that Ukrainian military intelligence used them. This isn’t the first time that civilian data centers have also been hit by drones and missiles. AWS sites in Bahrain and the UAE have been hit multiple times since Washington started its bombing campaign against Iran, with the company telling its clients to move their data to sites outside the region, as it doesn’t have a recovery timeline. items.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机袭击重创“俄罗斯谷歌”多个数据中心，Yandex机器人流量一夜之间几乎清零
items.descriptionZh:
乌克兰无人机对俄罗斯科技巨头Yandex数据中心的连续打击，正在显著削弱俄罗斯的互联网、云服务和后台计算能力。Yandex常被称为“俄罗斯的谷歌”，其业务覆盖搜索引擎、云计算、邮件、地图、流媒体和企业IT等关键数字服务。此次事件不仅是俄乌冲突中无人机远程打击的又一次升级，也把数据中心、超级计算机等数字基础设施推到了战争前线。

背景上，俄乌冲突在2022年俄罗斯试图攻占基辅失败后急剧升级，但不少观察者认为战争实际始于2014年俄罗斯夺取克里米亚并占领乌克兰东部部分地区。多年冲突推动了无人机战争的快速演化：早期主要是商用无人机执行侦察、投掷爆炸物和“神风”式攻击，随后发展为远程打击，专门制造的无人机可飞行超过1500英里，攻击远离前线的Tu-95战略轰炸机等目标。对数据中心的无人机打击则是较新的发展。俄方曾辩称，攻击乌克兰民用数据中心是因为乌军情报部门使用这些设施；而乌克兰对Yandex数据中心的攻击，显然是对莫斯科打击乌克兰数据中心的回应，后者曾导致一些热门盗版网站宕机。文中还提到，民用数据中心遭无人机和导弹袭击并非首次，例如AWS在巴林和阿联酋的站点自美国对伊朗发动轰炸行动以来多次被击中，AWS已建议客户将数据迁出该地区，且未给出恢复时间表。

从技术原理看，这类攻击的核心并非芯片设计或AI算法创新，而是对数据中心物理基础设施的精确摧毁。现代云服务依赖电力、冷却、光纤骨干网、边界路由和多地冗余。一旦供电、冷却或网络节点同时受损，软件层面的冗余和故障转移也可能失效，导致云服务状态页大面积报错。第三方监测机构则通过全球网络观测来量化损害：Cloudflare发现，来自Yandex网络的机器人流量已降至过去两周记录到的最大HTTP请求量的仅0.4%；在10月8日乌克兰首次击中位于俄罗斯萨索沃、距克里姆林宫东南约195英里、部署有两台超级计算机的Yandex数据中心时，该流量曾先降至约57%。随后，位于萨索沃以西约220英里的更大Yandex园区卡卢加数据中心昨日被打击离线，昨夜又发生了第三次攻击。NetBlocks确认，在乌克兰无人机今晨袭击弗拉基米尔的数据中心后，Yandex网络出现第二次崩溃；这一系列行动发生在俄罗斯威胁让乌克兰“数字排毒”后不久。

性能与对比数据方面，Yandex Cloud服务状态报告至少84项服务当前离线。全球互联网监测机构NetBlocks表示，Yandex Cloud的网络流量已降至仅30%，Yandex LLC的流量降至63%，这很可能导致普通俄罗斯用户遭遇互联网服务变慢甚至完全中断。更糟糕的是，普通俄罗斯用户无法像部分国家那样用高速卫星互联网作为备份，因为Starlink在俄罗斯不可用；而俄罗斯竞争对手的Rassvet卫星星座，已有相当数量在发射后坠回地面。

技术影响和应用场景上，这次打击直接冲击俄罗斯的云服务、搜索、邮件、地图、流媒体和企业IT系统，并可能波及部署在数据中心内的高性能计算/超算资源。对全球云厂商和关键基础设施运营者而言，这提供了重要警示：在地区冲突和混合战争中，数据中心已成为合法或事实上的打击目标，军民界限日益模糊；地理冗余、灾备、卫星通信备份、抗物理打击能力和供应链韧性必须重新评估。AWS在中东的先例也说明，区域冲突可能迫使云客户迁移数据，而恢复时间无法保证。整体来看，乌克兰对Yandex数据中心的连续无人机打击，既是俄乌数字基础设施战的一次升级，也展示了远程无人机、网络流量监测和云服务中断评估在现代战争中的结合方式。

items.title: Sandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD Review: Endurance at a premium
items.description: The Sandisk NAS 800 is a high-end PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD built for NAS workloads, with high endurance, strong sustained write performance, and low 4KB random latency. It’s mainly held back by its high price.
items.content: Sandisk is back with another welcome SSD, the NAS 800. As the name implies, this drive is designed for NAS appliances, but could also be a good choice for high-end desktop and enthusiast workstations. We recently reviewed the Optimus GX Pro 850P, a consumer drive for the PS5, so SanDisk is on a roll. The company has made it clear it wants to support the broader consumer market, as it’s even bringing back SATA SSDs in the form of the 320 and 520 series. The NAS 800 is closer in theme to the WD Red series of drives, like the WD Red SN700, which are optimized for home and small-business servers.At its heart, the NAS 800 is a specialized, optimized Sandisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 (formerly the WD Black SN8100). That progenitor is one of the best drives on the market. It has a stellar controller and excellent all-around flash with good power efficiency and low latency. This makes a great base for a NAS drive, although some changes are necessary. The bones are good, though, and this drive could be used in any system. The only real issue is that you’re paying a premium for the NAS optimizations, and that’s where our focus is.Sandisk NAS 800 Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally Product 960GB 1.92TB 3.84TB 7.68TB Pricing $387.99 $699.99 $1,374.99 $2,749.99 Form Factor M.2 2280-S3-M M.2 2280-S3-M M.2 2280-S3-M M.2 2280-D5-M Interface / Protocol PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 Controller SMI SM2508 SMI SM2508 SMI SM2508 SMI SM2508 DRAM Yes Yes Yes Yes Memory Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sequential Read 14,900 MB/s 14,900 MB/s 14,900 MB/s 14,900 MB/s Sequential Write 11,000 MB/s 13,200 MB/s 13,100 MB/s 13,000 MB/s Random Read 1,600K 2,300K 2,300K 2,200K Random Write 800K 1,500K 2,000K 2,100K Security TCG Opal TCG Opal TCG Opal TCG Opal Endurance (TBW) 1,750TB 3,500TB 7,000TB 14,000TB Part Number SDSNP2960GAN-000E0 SDSNP2192TAN-000E0 SDSNP2384TAN-000E0 SDSNP2768TAN-000E0 Height Not specified Not specified Not specified Not specified Warranty 5-Year 5-Year 5-Year 5-Year Today's best Sandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD deals $559.99ViewWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricesSandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD (SSD) at Amazon for $559.99The Sandisk NAS 800 has some strange capacities, at least compared to consumer offerings, because the drives reserve more spare flash as overprovisioning, which improves endurance. The drive comes in 960GB, 1.92TB, 3.84TB, and 7.68TB flavors. The final one is the most welcome, as it’s been difficult to find larger drives outside of enterprise. Performance is excellent, at up to 14,900 / 13,200 MB/s for sequential reads and writes and up to 2,300K / 2,100K random read and write IOPS. Peak overall performance should be achieved at 3.84TB.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Write endurance is where this drive really stands out. It’s rated for up to 14PBW at its maximum capacity. Proportional to size, this puts it at almost three times the normal for consumer drives. The drive also supports TCG Opal self-encryption for data at rest, as would be expected for a drive in this class. Things are capped off with a standard five-year warranty.You pay for this performance and endurance. At the time of writing,SanDisk’ss store lists the four capacities at $387.99, $699.99, $1,374.99, and $2,749.99. That’s roughly 45% to 65% more than the WD Black SN8100’s current street prices. Against the same drive under its new Optimus GX Pro 8100 name, the premium is between 27% and 29% at the time of review. The extra cost comes partly from the drive’s optimization but mostly from its TBW rating. You’re getting about one drive write per day over the five-year warranty, which is all but required for a drive of this type, and worthy of the price tag if you’re focused on endurance.Sandisk NAS 800 Software and AccessoriesIf you own a Sandisk drive, or a WD drive for that matter, then you should be no stranger to the NAS 800’s software offerings. Sandisk has its own dashboard, aptly named Sandisk Dashboard, which follows the popular WD Dashboard. This SSD toolbox has all the information you need for your drive, including important SMART and health information. It also lets you enable optional features, find firmware updates, and more. Sandisk also provides a download for its OEM version of Acronis True Image, useful for backing up your files or cloning your drive.Sandisk NAS 800: A Closer Look Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original The 1,920GB, or 1.92TB, version of the NAS 800 is single-sided. That also applies to the 960GB and 3.84TB versions. Only the 7.68TB version is double-sided, although that shouldn’t generally preclude you from using it in devices that would benefit from the drive. It could make a difference for certain cooling arrangements. The drive’s rating of 3.3V / 2.7A puts it at around 9W, which is between the drive’s maximum power state of 9.50W and its 6.5W / 6.4W average draw for this capacity. The reported active draw of 7.52W is higher than this average, but given that this drive is NAS-optimized with a small pseudo-SLC (pSLC) cache, it will likely be lower in practice. The drive should run cooler as a result.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original The drive layout includes the SSD controller, a DRAM package, and two NAND flash packages. The 7.68TB version will need more packages on the rear, for a total of four flash packages. The controller is labeled in a way similar to SanDisk’s proprietary parts, but the “250800” spells out that this is a Silicon Motion, or SMI, SM2508. This is an eight-channel, high-end PCIe 5.0 SSD controller with generally excellent performance and power efficiency.The DRAM package is LPDDR4 and is therefore a more power-efficient choice. It’s also 2GB, which follows the normal 1:1,000 ratio of DRAM to NAND. Our recent Optimus GX Pro 850P review had a 2TB drive from Sandisk with only 1GB of RAM. That’s perfectly suitable for gaming use. For this NAS drive, 2GB is very much preferred. The controller and DRAM are paired with SanDisk’s 218-layer BiCS8 TLC flash. This is some of the best flash on the market, with good all-around performance, very good latency, and very good power efficiency. items.titleZh: Sandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD 评测：耐久性需高价换取
items.descriptionZh:
Sandisk 推出了新款 SSD——NAS 800，从命名即可看出它主要面向 NAS 设备，但同样适合高端台式机和发烧级工作站。此前，Sandisk 刚刚评测了面向 PS5 的消费级产品 Optimus GX Pro 850P，并明确表示要支持更广泛的消费市场，甚至以 320 和 520 系列重新带回 SATA SSD。NAS 800 在定位上更接近 WD Red 系列，例如 WD Red SN700，专门针对家庭和小型企业服务器进行优化。它的核心基础是 Sandisk Optimus GX Pro 8100，也就是原来的 WD Black SN8100。后者本就是市场上最好的 SSD 之一，拥有出色的控制器、优秀的闪存整体表现、良好的能效和低延迟，因此非常适合作为 NAS 硬盘的基础，只需针对 NAS 场景做部分调整。虽然用户也可以把它用在任何系统中，但问题在于，你需要为这些 NAS 优化支付溢价。

从规格看，NAS 800 提供 960GB、1.92TB、3.84TB 和 7.68TB 四种容量，官方定价分别为 387.99 美元、699.99 美元、1374.99 美元和 2749.99 美元。它采用 M.2 2280 外形，其中 7.68TB 版本为 M.2 2280-D5-M，其余为 M.2 2280-S3-M；接口为 PCIe 5.0 x4、NVMe 2.0；控制器为 SMI SM2508；配备 DRAM 缓存；闪存为 Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND；支持 TCG Opal 自加密；提供 5 年保修。性能方面，全系顺序读取最高可达 14,900 MB/s，顺序写入分别为 11,000、13,200、13,100 和 13,000 MB/s；随机读取分别为 1,600K、2,300K、2,300K 和 2,200K IOPS；随机写入分别为 800K、1,500K、2,000K 和 2,100K IOPS。整体峰值性能预计出现在 3.84TB 版本。

这些容量看起来有些“奇怪”，是因为硬盘预留了更多备用闪存作为 overprovisioning，从而提升耐久度。其中 7.68TB 版本最受欢迎，因为企业级之外的大容量 SSD 一直比较难找。写入耐久是 NAS 800 真正的亮点：最大容量版本额定耐久高达 14PBW，按容量比例计算，大约是普通消费级 SSD 的三倍。它还支持 TCG Opal 自加密，适合需要静态数据保护的环境。当然，这些性能和耐久都有代价。按评测时价格，它比 WD Black SN8100 的当前街价高约 45% 到 65%；即使与更名后的 Optimus GX Pro 8100 相比，溢价也在 27% 到 29% 左右。额外成本一部分来自 NAS 优化，但主要来自 TBW 耐久评级。换算下来，五年保修期内大约相当于每天全盘写入一次，这对这类硬盘几乎可以说是必需，如果你看重耐久，这个价格是值得的。

在软件和附件方面，NAS 800 延续了 Sandisk 和 WD 硬盘的生态。Sandisk 提供名为 Sandisk Dashboard 的工具，类似于 WD Dashboard，可查看 SMART 和健康信息，启用可选功能，查找固件更新等。Sandisk 还提供 OEM 版 Acronis True Image 下载，用于备份文件或克隆硬盘。物理设计上，960GB、1.92TB 和 3.84TB 版本均为单面，仅 7.68TB 版本为双面，这可能影响某些散热配置。其额定功耗为 3.3V / 2.7A，约 9W，介于最大 9.50W 和平均 6.5W / 6.4W 之间；报告的活动功耗为 7.52W，高于平均值，但由于该盘针对 NAS 优化且只配备较小的伪 SLC 缓存，实际功耗可能更低，运行温度也会更凉。硬盘布局包括 SSD 控制器、一个 DRAM 封装和两个 NAND 闪存封装；7.68TB 版本需要在背面增加封装，总共四个闪存封装。控制器标记中的“250800”表明这是 Silicon Motion 的 SM2508，一款八通道高端 PCIe 5.0 SSD 控制器，性能和能效总体出色。DRAM 为 LPDDR4，能效更高，容量 2GB，符合 DRAM 与 NAND 约 1:1000 的常规比例。相比之下，最近评测的 Optimus GX Pro 850P 中，2TB 版本只有 1GB RAM，适合游戏；而对 NAS 硬盘来说，2GB 更受青睐。控制器和 DRAM 搭配的是 Sandisk 218 层 BiCS8 TLC 闪存，这是市场上最好的闪存之一，整体性能、延迟和能效都很优秀。可以说，这是世界级硬件，价格也反映了这一点。

总体来看，Sandisk NAS 800 的意义在于，它把高端 PCIe 5.0 M.2 SSD 的性能与 NAS 所需的高耐久、自加密和持续写入优化结合起来，为家庭和小型企业服务器、高端台式机、发烧级工作站以及需要高 TBW 的用户提供了一个新选择。它也表明 Sandisk 正在扩大在消费级和专业消费者存储市场的存在，并试图用高耐久 M.2 产品切入原本由企业级或 WD Red 系列覆盖的 NAS 场景。不过，它的价格明显高于同源消费级产品，更适合那些真正需要高耐久、数据静止加密和 PCIe 5.0 性能，而不是单纯追求性价比的用户。

items.content: I’m embarking on a journey I’ve so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it’s increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they’re capable of. Is this tech so useful that it’s worth throwing gobs of money at a computer or a laptop with lots of overpriced RAM? I’ll try to help you find out. I’m not an AI expert, it’s going to be a journey for me, but maybe I can help you see if that journey is worth taking — and I’ll be posting my way through it.A big part of Apple’s pitch for its new Mac desktops is how good they are for local AI, and there’s an entire line of new RTX Spark Windows machines landing imminently with up to 128GB of RAM aimed at using agentic AI. Local AI and agents are just, like, so hot right now. But, in all seriousness, the thought of having a little gofer living solely in the box on my desk that answers only to me and not overlords from OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, or Anthropic hits a bit different than trusting cloud services or subscribing to a chatbot. Don’t get me wrong, there’s still no way I’m gonna have it write for me, edit for me, or generate ugly fliers. But now, with some privacy on my side maybe I can finally think of useful busy work to “trust” it with.So as part of my ongoing testing of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, as well as experimenting on other Mac and Windows systems, I’ve installed some local LLMs and I’m beginning to tinker. Here’s how things are going.PreviousNext1/4Hermes Agent can be used with cloud or local models.I started by installing the open-source Hermes Agent on the Mac Studio. Hermes is a self-hosted AI agent desktop app that works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It’s completely free to use if you stick to local LLMs. Since this M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256GB of unified memory, I could run just about any model I want. This is how things quickly get overwhelming. There are more models out there than I can count, and some have specialized uses. Generally, models with many billions of parameters are able to do more than smaller ones with only a few billion. And since we don’t have to worry about paying for tokens when running a model locally, I figured I’d go big to start.Using Hermes’ straightforward onboarding interface and model picker, I chose the Qwen 3.8 Flash Next model — a 125-billion parameter model that’s around 105GB in size. I also plan on spending some time with much smaller Qwen models on devices like an M6 Mac Mini, M5 MacBook Air, an Asus TUF Gaming A14 with AMD Strix Halo processor, and, eventually, RTX Spark. (Care to share what local models and hardware you use? You know where to leave your comments. 🫡)It wasn’t long to get up and running with Hermes and Qwen, and even make them controllable via my phone by using a Telegram bot. But then, I was presented with my usual nemesis when it comes to using AI: the text box.“What do I do with this thing?”My Hermes daily briefing, sent to me daily via Telegram. Basic, I know.First up, to get things going, I followed some helpful YouTube advice and had Hermes make me a daily morning briefing — to just start small with a cron job and ensure things are working. It scans my email and calendar, tells me anything worth my immediate attention, and gives me a short weather report. It’s not all that useful, and you obviously don’t need a $12,000 computer to build it, but it’s something I can develop over time. The brief kept failing to generate at first, but then I eventually figured out that macOS couldn’t be asleep when the job fired up at 7:30am. Duh! It works like clockwork now, but I have to think of more info for it to pull for me to make the results more helpful.A more useful task was reorganizing my Steam library. I have over 400 games on Steam, and I recently started categorizing them for when I want to play something new on a whim. Steam doesn’t categorize your games for you, so you instead have to do it manually, one-by-one. But here’s where an agentic lackey could fit right in. I asked, “Can you reorganize my Steam library?” Hermes could see most of my games by just viewing the already installed Steam client. It quickly came up with some organization options for me. I decided to have it organize my games by genre, but leave some of my own specialized categories(favorites, co-op titles, party games, games to play with my wife, etc.).You have to give a local AI some permissions over your machine for it to take actions for you, and in the case of my game library I had to register a Steam web API key and give it to Hermes. Once it had that access, it only took a few minutes for it to churn through sorting all the games into categories. And the API key was easy to revoke right after, since I don’t need it further. The idea is for it to just do this heavy lifting for me once, and then I’ll file new games into the categories as I eventually buy them. It did a fine job overall, and now my Steam library is easily browsable.PreviousNext1/2Starting the process of having Hermes organize my Steam library.Another simple thing I did was data analysis. I had Hermes take a look at financial records to crunch some numbers for me, and I also had it make me a spec comparison spreadsheet for a new laptop. These are small things, but they’re both tasks I cannot or will not trust with any cloud service — I don’t want to upload that sensitive data to the cloud, and in the case of a new laptop, that info was under embargo. Keeping them on my computer was the difference in me using this tool or not.The bigger bit of automation I’m currently working on is a script to run a series of laptop benchmark tests. I run all our benchmarks manually, and tending to a laptop to run a dozen or so tests — three times over, to take the average — is incredibly time-consuming. I’d love to automate at least some of it. Even walking Hermes through all of the required procedures and getting it to spit out vibe coded Python scripts has been a bit of an endeavor, and it remains a work in progress. But I’m hoping to make some positive headway.Apple demoed this cluster of four Mac Studios wired up in a cluster for local AI at a briefing I attended last month. That’s nearly $50,000 worth of compute.It’s still early days of me working with Hermes, and I’m hoping this is just the tip of the iceberg on the useful things I get it to do for me. But it’s also clear that even these powerful local models don’t make for a magical assistant that can do anything. Things still don’t always work as intended — my daily briefing already broke, multiple times.I view Hermes and local AI as just a tool, a computer program to run on my computer. I don’t want a digital friend. I’m not saying “thank you” or “please,” or typing “sorry” when I change my mind on something. I’m remaining as stone-cold and indifferent when ordering it around as I am clicking a mouse around an operating system.I hope to remain vigilant and cautious while I continue testing and learning with local AI. Let’s see where it takes me.

items.titleZh: 学习使用本地AI既令人兴奋，又让人不知所措，还令人沮丧
items.descriptionZh:
本文作者以第一人称记录了自己从对云端AI的隐私顾虑出发，开始尝试在本地设备上运行大模型和AI代理的历程。背景是，Apple在新款Mac桌面电脑的宣传中大力强调其本地AI能力；与此同时，即将上市的一整条RTX Spark Windows整机产品线最高配备128GB内存，面向代理式AI（agentic AI）。本地AI和AI代理正成为热点。作者一直不愿把最私密的数据交给云服务，也不愿依赖OpenAI、Google、Microsoft或Anthropic等云端聊天机器人，因此想验证：本地模型是否已经强大到值得为一台电脑或笔记本投入大笔金钱，尤其是为高价内存买单。作者强调自己并非AI专家，但希望把这段探索过程分享出来。

作者的核心测试平台是M5 Ultra Mac Studio，配备256GB统一内存。他在上面安装了开源的Hermes Agent。Hermes是一个自托管的AI代理桌面应用，支持macOS、Windows和Linux，如果只搭配本地LLM使用则完全免费。由于256GB统一内存足以运行几乎所有想跑的模型，作者选择了Qwen 3.8 Flash Next——一个约1250亿参数、体积约105GB的模型。文章解释，通常参数规模越大的模型能力越强，而本地运行无需按token付费，因此作者决定“从大开始”。他也计划在M6 Mac Mini、M5 MacBook Air、搭载AMD Strix Halo处理器的Asus TUF Gaming A14，以及未来的RTX Spark上测试更小的Qwen模型。Hermes的上手界面和模型选择器比较简单，作者还通过Telegram bot让手机也能控制它。

不过，真正开始用后，作者很快遇到老问题：面对文本框，“我该拿它做什么？”他先按YouTube建议让Hermes生成每日晨报：扫描邮件和日历，提示需要立即关注的事项，并给出一段简短天气报告。这个功能一开始失败，后来发现是macOS在早上7:30任务触发时不能处于睡眠状态。问题解决后，晨报能像时钟一样运行，但作者认为它并不算特别有用，也不需要一台1.2万美元的电脑才能实现，只是可以作为长期迭代的基础。

更实用的任务是整理Steam游戏库。作者有400多款Steam游戏，Steam本身不自动分类，只能手动逐个整理。他让Hermes“重新组织Steam库”，Hermes通过查看已安装的Steam客户端识别大部分游戏，并快速给出分类方案。作者选择按类型分类，同时保留自己的特殊分类，如最爱、合作游戏、派对游戏、与妻子一起玩的游戏等。要让本地AI替自己操作电脑，必须授予一定权限；整理游戏库时，作者注册了Steam Web API密钥并交给Hermes。获得权限后，Hermes几分钟就完成了分类，随后作者立即撤销了密钥，因为不再需要。作者希望这种重活只做一次，以后新买的游戏再自行归档。

作者还用Hermes做数据分析：让它查看财务记录并计算数字，以及为新笔记本制作规格对比表格。这些任务虽小，但都是他不能或不愿交给云服务的——财务数据过于敏感，而新笔记本信息当时还处于禁运期。把数据保留在本地，是作者是否使用这类工具的关键区别。目前他正在推进更大的自动化项目：编写脚本自动运行一系列笔记本基准测试。作者平时手动跑所有基准测试，一台笔记本要跑十几项测试、重复三次取平均，非常耗时。他希望至少自动化一部分。即使只是让Hermes理解所有流程并生成“凭感觉写的”Python脚本，也已经相当费劲，目前仍在进行中。

文章还提到，Apple曾在一场简报会上演示用四台Mac Studio组成集群运行本地AI，这套算力价值近5万美元。作者认为，自己与Hermes的相处仍处于早期，希望目前这些只是冰山一角。但也很清楚，即使强大的本地模型也不是能包办一切的魔法助手，事情并不总按预期运行，他的每日晨报就已经坏过多次。作者把Hermes和本地AI视为电脑上的一个工具、一个程序，而不是数字朋友；他不会说“谢谢”“请”，改变主意时也不会打“抱歉”，而是像点击操作系统鼠标一样冷静、无动于衷地下指令。他希望在继续测试和学习本地AI的过程中保持警惕和谨慎。

整体来看，这篇文章反映了本地AI与AI代理浪潮中的几个关键问题：隐私和数据主权推动了本地运行需求；Apple Silicon的大统一内存和即将到来的RTX Spark Windows机器，把大内存作为本地AI的核心卖点；本地LLM可按参数规模和模型体积选择，1250亿参数、105GB模型在256GB内存设备上可运行，且无token费用，但硬件成本高；代理式AI可以执行邮件简报、Steam库整理、财务分析、规格表生成和基准测试自动化等任务，但需要授予权限、处理API密钥，并面对可靠性和工作流搭建门槛。对不愿上传敏感数据、未公开信息或希望拥有“只听从自己”的AI的用户来说，本地AI正在成为云服务之外的真实选项，但它距离成熟、稳定、易用的个人智能助手仍有距离。

history.content: When President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” you’d be forgiven for being skeptical that it would catch on. While most of the broader population is sticking with AI, some of Silicon Valley’s most powerful are falling in line and trying to give Trump the great AI rebrand he so desires.That Elon Musk was quick to jump on board, promising to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, isn’t surprising. When, hours after Donald Trump declared that “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!” Marc Benioff announced that Salesforce would rename AIForce to SIForce; it seemed like a quick capitulation, but not entirely out of character.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the summit where the executive order requiring government agencies to use the term “super intelligence” was announced. He’s also aligned himself with Trump, saying he believes the danger posed by AI is overblown. So it was somewhat predictable that when Nvidia declared that it would “commit” $1 billion to scientific advancement, that included “super intelligence research.” Of course, Huang has a lot to lose if he gets on Trump’s bad side.The latest to cave is Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, who attended the same AI summit as Huang along with Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai, Jeff Bezos, Dario Amodei, and Musk. In a post calling for building an “emergency brake” for AI yesterday, Nadella repeatedly referred to the technology as “super intelligence.”During Trump’s second term, Silicon Valley has repeatedly tried to ingratiate itself with the administration, after having a much more contentious relationship during his first term.

history.titleZh: 硅谷与特朗普改写人工智能的企图保持一致
history.descriptionZh:
报道称，特朗普政府正推动把“人工智能”（AI）改称为“超级智能”（Super Intelligence），并试图让这一新术语进入官方话语。文章描述，特朗普不仅宣布要重塑AI的名称，还宣称白宫会把继续使用“人工智能”一词的人视为“敌人”，并签署行政命令要求政府机构采用“超级智能”这一所谓“更准确”的表述。尽管公众仍普遍使用AI，但硅谷部分最有影响力的高管正在配合这一改名运动。

背景是，特朗普第二任期内，硅谷与政府的关系明显转向。经历了第一任期的紧张和对抗后，科技公司和高管频繁向政府靠拢，希望在监管、采购、补贴和政策环境中获得有利位置。因此，当特朗普推动AI改名时，一些科技领袖迅速跟进，把这当作政治站队和公关表态。

具体案例包括：马斯克迅速响应，承诺把“SpaceXAI”改名为“SpaceXSI”；Salesforce的马克·贝尼奥夫宣布将“AIForce”改为“SIForce”，被文章视为快速妥协。英伟达CEO黄仁勋出席了宣布相关行政命令的峰会，并曾表示AI带来的危险被夸大；英伟达随后宣布向科学进步“承诺”10亿美元，其中包含“超级智能研究”。文章指出，如果黄仁勋得罪特朗普，英伟达可能面临很大利益风险。最新跟进的是微软CEO萨提亚·纳德拉。他与黄仁勋、扎克伯格、皮查伊、贝索斯、Dario Amodei和马斯克等参加了同一场AI峰会，并在呼吁为AI建立“紧急刹车”的帖子中多次把该技术称为“超级智能”。

从技术角度看，这篇文章并没有发布新的芯片、模型或算法，也没有给出性能参数或对比数据；“超级智能”也不是一个已被实现的技术里程碑。通常，AI是更宽泛的术语，而“超级智能”指在几乎所有认知任务上超越人类水平的智能系统，目前仍属理论或远期概念。因此，把现有AI技术、治理和政策讨论统一改称“超级智能”，更像是一种话语重构和政治表态，可能夸大当前技术能力，并影响公众认知、监管框架、投资叙事以及政府项目命名。对AI芯片和算力行业而言，文中唯一可量化的动作是英伟达的10亿美元科学投入承诺；更广泛的影响则在于，政策术语变化可能牵动政府AI项目、研发资金、采购和监管沟通，但算力需求本身仍主要由模型规模、训练和推理部署等实际因素驱动。

history.title: Russia's Yandex bot traffic nearly eliminated overnight after Ukraine drone strikes cripple multiple of 'Russia's Google' data centers
history.description: Russian bot traffic falls dramatically as Ukraine takes out several Yandex data centers.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Russian bot traffic has dropped dramatically in the past few days after Ukraine knocked out Yandex’s biggest data centers, with a third attack happening last night. Cloudflare reports that bot traffic from the Yandex network has dropped to just 0.4% of the maximum number of HTTP requests recorded in the past two weeks. It initially dropped to around 57% on Oct. 8, which happened when Ukraine hit a Yandex data center housing two supercomputers in Sasovo, Russia, located around 195 miles to the southeast of the Kremlin. A second, bigger Yandex campus in Kaluga, about 220 miles to the west of Sasovo, was knocked offline yesterday. These attacks are apparently Ukraine’s response to Moscow’s strikes on its own data centers, some of which resulted in the outage of some of the most popular piracy websites. (Image credit: CloudFlare)Yandex is Russia’s equivalent to Google, and its Yandex Cloud service status reports that at least 84 services are currently offline. Global internet monitoring firm NetBlocks said that Yandex’s network traffic has dropped to just 30% for Yandex Cloud and 63% for Yandex LLC, most likely resulting in slower internet services or complete disruption for the average Russian. Unfortunately, the ordinary Russian wouldn’t be able to use high-speed satellite internet as a backup, as Starlink does not work in Russia, while the competing Rassvet constellation has had a good number of its existing satellites fall back to the surface after launch.⚠️ Confirmed: Metrics show a second collapse in the networks of Russian tech giant Yandex after a new Ukrainian drone attack on data centers in Vladimir this morning. The campaign comes not long after Russia's threat to give Ukraine a "digital detox." https://t.co/jOVL5BjYNROctober 11, 2026These incidents are a result of the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, which escalated dramatically in 2022 after Russia’s failed attempt to capture Kyiv. However, many observers say that the war actually started in 2014 when Russian forces seized Crimea and occupied parts of eastern Ukraine after the fall of the pro-Russian government that year.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The hostilities, which have dragged on for years, saw the introduction of new technologies and strategies, specifically in drone warfare. It began with the wide deployment of commercially available drones on the front lines, typically for reconnaissance, dropping explosives, and kamikaze-style attacks. However, it has since evolved into long-range warfare, with specially built drones able to reach distances of over 1,500 miles and destroy Tu-95 strategic bombers situated well behind the front lines.The drone strikes on data centers are relatively new developments. While data centers on bases are often considered valid targets, Russia’s justification for the attacks on civilian data centers was that Ukrainian military intelligence used them. This isn’t the first time that civilian data centers have also been hit by drones and missiles. AWS sites in Bahrain and the UAE have been hit multiple times since Washington started its bombing campaign against Iran, with the company telling its clients to move their data to sites outside the region, as it doesn’t have a recovery timeline. history.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机袭击重创“俄罗斯谷歌”多个数据中心，Yandex机器人流量一夜之间几乎清零
history.descriptionZh:
乌克兰无人机对俄罗斯科技巨头Yandex数据中心的连续打击，正在显著削弱俄罗斯的互联网、云服务和后台计算能力。Yandex常被称为“俄罗斯的谷歌”，其业务覆盖搜索引擎、云计算、邮件、地图、流媒体和企业IT等关键数字服务。此次事件不仅是俄乌冲突中无人机远程打击的又一次升级，也把数据中心、超级计算机等数字基础设施推到了战争前线。

背景上，俄乌冲突在2022年俄罗斯试图攻占基辅失败后急剧升级，但不少观察者认为战争实际始于2014年俄罗斯夺取克里米亚并占领乌克兰东部部分地区。多年冲突推动了无人机战争的快速演化：早期主要是商用无人机执行侦察、投掷爆炸物和“神风”式攻击，随后发展为远程打击，专门制造的无人机可飞行超过1500英里，攻击远离前线的Tu-95战略轰炸机等目标。对数据中心的无人机打击则是较新的发展。俄方曾辩称，攻击乌克兰民用数据中心是因为乌军情报部门使用这些设施；而乌克兰对Yandex数据中心的攻击，显然是对莫斯科打击乌克兰数据中心的回应，后者曾导致一些热门盗版网站宕机。文中还提到，民用数据中心遭无人机和导弹袭击并非首次，例如AWS在巴林和阿联酋的站点自美国对伊朗发动轰炸行动以来多次被击中，AWS已建议客户将数据迁出该地区，且未给出恢复时间表。

从技术原理看，这类攻击的核心并非芯片设计或AI算法创新，而是对数据中心物理基础设施的精确摧毁。现代云服务依赖电力、冷却、光纤骨干网、边界路由和多地冗余。一旦供电、冷却或网络节点同时受损，软件层面的冗余和故障转移也可能失效，导致云服务状态页大面积报错。第三方监测机构则通过全球网络观测来量化损害：Cloudflare发现，来自Yandex网络的机器人流量已降至过去两周记录到的最大HTTP请求量的仅0.4%；在10月8日乌克兰首次击中位于俄罗斯萨索沃、距克里姆林宫东南约195英里、部署有两台超级计算机的Yandex数据中心时，该流量曾先降至约57%。随后，位于萨索沃以西约220英里的更大Yandex园区卡卢加数据中心昨日被打击离线，昨夜又发生了第三次攻击。NetBlocks确认，在乌克兰无人机今晨袭击弗拉基米尔的数据中心后，Yandex网络出现第二次崩溃；这一系列行动发生在俄罗斯威胁让乌克兰“数字排毒”后不久。

性能与对比数据方面，Yandex Cloud服务状态报告至少84项服务当前离线。全球互联网监测机构NetBlocks表示，Yandex Cloud的网络流量已降至仅30%，Yandex LLC的流量降至63%，这很可能导致普通俄罗斯用户遭遇互联网服务变慢甚至完全中断。更糟糕的是，普通俄罗斯用户无法像部分国家那样用高速卫星互联网作为备份，因为Starlink在俄罗斯不可用；而俄罗斯竞争对手的Rassvet卫星星座，已有相当数量在发射后坠回地面。

技术影响和应用场景上，这次打击直接冲击俄罗斯的云服务、搜索、邮件、地图、流媒体和企业IT系统，并可能波及部署在数据中心内的高性能计算/超算资源。对全球云厂商和关键基础设施运营者而言，这提供了重要警示：在地区冲突和混合战争中，数据中心已成为合法或事实上的打击目标，军民界限日益模糊；地理冗余、灾备、卫星通信备份、抗物理打击能力和供应链韧性必须重新评估。AWS在中东的先例也说明，区域冲突可能迫使云客户迁移数据，而恢复时间无法保证。整体来看，乌克兰对Yandex数据中心的连续无人机打击，既是俄乌数字基础设施战的一次升级，也展示了远程无人机、网络流量监测和云服务中断评估在现代战争中的结合方式。

history.title: Sandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD Review: Endurance at a premium
history.description: The Sandisk NAS 800 is a high-end PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD built for NAS workloads, with high endurance, strong sustained write performance, and low 4KB random latency. It’s mainly held back by its high price.
history.content: Sandisk is back with another welcome SSD, the NAS 800. As the name implies, this drive is designed for NAS appliances, but could also be a good choice for high-end desktop and enthusiast workstations. We recently reviewed the Optimus GX Pro 850P, a consumer drive for the PS5, so SanDisk is on a roll. The company has made it clear it wants to support the broader consumer market, as it’s even bringing back SATA SSDs in the form of the 320 and 520 series. The NAS 800 is closer in theme to the WD Red series of drives, like the WD Red SN700, which are optimized for home and small-business servers.At its heart, the NAS 800 is a specialized, optimized Sandisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 (formerly the WD Black SN8100). That progenitor is one of the best drives on the market. It has a stellar controller and excellent all-around flash with good power efficiency and low latency. This makes a great base for a NAS drive, although some changes are necessary. The bones are good, though, and this drive could be used in any system. The only real issue is that you’re paying a premium for the NAS optimizations, and that’s where our focus is.Sandisk NAS 800 Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally Product 960GB 1.92TB 3.84TB 7.68TB Pricing $387.99 $699.99 $1,374.99 $2,749.99 Form Factor M.2 2280-S3-M M.2 2280-S3-M M.2 2280-S3-M M.2 2280-D5-M Interface / Protocol PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 PCIe 5.0 x4 / NVMe 2.0 Controller SMI SM2508 SMI SM2508 SMI SM2508 SMI SM2508 DRAM Yes Yes Yes Yes Memory Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND Sequential Read 14,900 MB/s 14,900 MB/s 14,900 MB/s 14,900 MB/s Sequential Write 11,000 MB/s 13,200 MB/s 13,100 MB/s 13,000 MB/s Random Read 1,600K 2,300K 2,300K 2,200K Random Write 800K 1,500K 2,000K 2,100K Security TCG Opal TCG Opal TCG Opal TCG Opal Endurance (TBW) 1,750TB 3,500TB 7,000TB 14,000TB Part Number SDSNP2960GAN-000E0 SDSNP2192TAN-000E0 SDSNP2384TAN-000E0 SDSNP2768TAN-000E0 Height Not specified Not specified Not specified Not specified Warranty 5-Year 5-Year 5-Year 5-Year Today's best Sandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD deals $559.99ViewWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricesSandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD (SSD) at Amazon for $559.99The Sandisk NAS 800 has some strange capacities, at least compared to consumer offerings, because the drives reserve more spare flash as overprovisioning, which improves endurance. The drive comes in 960GB, 1.92TB, 3.84TB, and 7.68TB flavors. The final one is the most welcome, as it’s been difficult to find larger drives outside of enterprise. Performance is excellent, at up to 14,900 / 13,200 MB/s for sequential reads and writes and up to 2,300K / 2,100K random read and write IOPS. Peak overall performance should be achieved at 3.84TB.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Write endurance is where this drive really stands out. It’s rated for up to 14PBW at its maximum capacity. Proportional to size, this puts it at almost three times the normal for consumer drives. The drive also supports TCG Opal self-encryption for data at rest, as would be expected for a drive in this class. Things are capped off with a standard five-year warranty.You pay for this performance and endurance. At the time of writing,SanDisk’ss store lists the four capacities at $387.99, $699.99, $1,374.99, and $2,749.99. That’s roughly 45% to 65% more than the WD Black SN8100’s current street prices. Against the same drive under its new Optimus GX Pro 8100 name, the premium is between 27% and 29% at the time of review. The extra cost comes partly from the drive’s optimization but mostly from its TBW rating. You’re getting about one drive write per day over the five-year warranty, which is all but required for a drive of this type, and worthy of the price tag if you’re focused on endurance.Sandisk NAS 800 Software and AccessoriesIf you own a Sandisk drive, or a WD drive for that matter, then you should be no stranger to the NAS 800’s software offerings. Sandisk has its own dashboard, aptly named Sandisk Dashboard, which follows the popular WD Dashboard. This SSD toolbox has all the information you need for your drive, including important SMART and health information. It also lets you enable optional features, find firmware updates, and more. Sandisk also provides a download for its OEM version of Acronis True Image, useful for backing up your files or cloning your drive.Sandisk NAS 800: A Closer Look Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original The 1,920GB, or 1.92TB, version of the NAS 800 is single-sided. That also applies to the 960GB and 3.84TB versions. Only the 7.68TB version is double-sided, although that shouldn’t generally preclude you from using it in devices that would benefit from the drive. It could make a difference for certain cooling arrangements. The drive’s rating of 3.3V / 2.7A puts it at around 9W, which is between the drive’s maximum power state of 9.50W and its 6.5W / 6.4W average draw for this capacity. The reported active draw of 7.52W is higher than this average, but given that this drive is NAS-optimized with a small pseudo-SLC (pSLC) cache, it will likely be lower in practice. The drive should run cooler as a result.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original The drive layout includes the SSD controller, a DRAM package, and two NAND flash packages. The 7.68TB version will need more packages on the rear, for a total of four flash packages. The controller is labeled in a way similar to SanDisk’s proprietary parts, but the “250800” spells out that this is a Silicon Motion, or SMI, SM2508. This is an eight-channel, high-end PCIe 5.0 SSD controller with generally excellent performance and power efficiency.The DRAM package is LPDDR4 and is therefore a more power-efficient choice. It’s also 2GB, which follows the normal 1:1,000 ratio of DRAM to NAND. Our recent Optimus GX Pro 850P review had a 2TB drive from Sandisk with only 1GB of RAM. That’s perfectly suitable for gaming use. For this NAS drive, 2GB is very much preferred. The controller and DRAM are paired with SanDisk’s 218-layer BiCS8 TLC flash. This is some of the best flash on the market, with good all-around performance, very good latency, and very good power efficiency. history.titleZh: Sandisk NAS 800 1.92TB SSD 评测：耐久性需高价换取
history.descriptionZh:
Sandisk 推出了新款 SSD——NAS 800，从命名即可看出它主要面向 NAS 设备，但同样适合高端台式机和发烧级工作站。此前，Sandisk 刚刚评测了面向 PS5 的消费级产品 Optimus GX Pro 850P，并明确表示要支持更广泛的消费市场，甚至以 320 和 520 系列重新带回 SATA SSD。NAS 800 在定位上更接近 WD Red 系列，例如 WD Red SN700，专门针对家庭和小型企业服务器进行优化。它的核心基础是 Sandisk Optimus GX Pro 8100，也就是原来的 WD Black SN8100。后者本就是市场上最好的 SSD 之一，拥有出色的控制器、优秀的闪存整体表现、良好的能效和低延迟，因此非常适合作为 NAS 硬盘的基础，只需针对 NAS 场景做部分调整。虽然用户也可以把它用在任何系统中，但问题在于，你需要为这些 NAS 优化支付溢价。

从规格看，NAS 800 提供 960GB、1.92TB、3.84TB 和 7.68TB 四种容量，官方定价分别为 387.99 美元、699.99 美元、1374.99 美元和 2749.99 美元。它采用 M.2 2280 外形，其中 7.68TB 版本为 M.2 2280-D5-M，其余为 M.2 2280-S3-M；接口为 PCIe 5.0 x4、NVMe 2.0；控制器为 SMI SM2508；配备 DRAM 缓存；闪存为 Sandisk TLC 3D CBA NAND；支持 TCG Opal 自加密；提供 5 年保修。性能方面，全系顺序读取最高可达 14,900 MB/s，顺序写入分别为 11,000、13,200、13,100 和 13,000 MB/s；随机读取分别为 1,600K、2,300K、2,300K 和 2,200K IOPS；随机写入分别为 800K、1,500K、2,000K 和 2,100K IOPS。整体峰值性能预计出现在 3.84TB 版本。

这些容量看起来有些“奇怪”，是因为硬盘预留了更多备用闪存作为 overprovisioning，从而提升耐久度。其中 7.68TB 版本最受欢迎，因为企业级之外的大容量 SSD 一直比较难找。写入耐久是 NAS 800 真正的亮点：最大容量版本额定耐久高达 14PBW，按容量比例计算，大约是普通消费级 SSD 的三倍。它还支持 TCG Opal 自加密，适合需要静态数据保护的环境。当然，这些性能和耐久都有代价。按评测时价格，它比 WD Black SN8100 的当前街价高约 45% 到 65%；即使与更名后的 Optimus GX Pro 8100 相比，溢价也在 27% 到 29% 左右。额外成本一部分来自 NAS 优化，但主要来自 TBW 耐久评级。换算下来，五年保修期内大约相当于每天全盘写入一次，这对这类硬盘几乎可以说是必需，如果你看重耐久，这个价格是值得的。

在软件和附件方面，NAS 800 延续了 Sandisk 和 WD 硬盘的生态。Sandisk 提供名为 Sandisk Dashboard 的工具，类似于 WD Dashboard，可查看 SMART 和健康信息，启用可选功能，查找固件更新等。Sandisk 还提供 OEM 版 Acronis True Image 下载，用于备份文件或克隆硬盘。物理设计上，960GB、1.92TB 和 3.84TB 版本均为单面，仅 7.68TB 版本为双面，这可能影响某些散热配置。其额定功耗为 3.3V / 2.7A，约 9W，介于最大 9.50W 和平均 6.5W / 6.4W 之间；报告的活动功耗为 7.52W，高于平均值，但由于该盘针对 NAS 优化且只配备较小的伪 SLC 缓存，实际功耗可能更低，运行温度也会更凉。硬盘布局包括 SSD 控制器、一个 DRAM 封装和两个 NAND 闪存封装；7.68TB 版本需要在背面增加封装，总共四个闪存封装。控制器标记中的“250800”表明这是 Silicon Motion 的 SM2508，一款八通道高端 PCIe 5.0 SSD 控制器，性能和能效总体出色。DRAM 为 LPDDR4，能效更高，容量 2GB，符合 DRAM 与 NAND 约 1:1000 的常规比例。相比之下，最近评测的 Optimus GX Pro 850P 中，2TB 版本只有 1GB RAM，适合游戏；而对 NAS 硬盘来说，2GB 更受青睐。控制器和 DRAM 搭配的是 Sandisk 218 层 BiCS8 TLC 闪存，这是市场上最好的闪存之一，整体性能、延迟和能效都很优秀。可以说，这是世界级硬件，价格也反映了这一点。

总体来看，Sandisk NAS 800 的意义在于，它把高端 PCIe 5.0 M.2 SSD 的性能与 NAS 所需的高耐久、自加密和持续写入优化结合起来，为家庭和小型企业服务器、高端台式机、发烧级工作站以及需要高 TBW 的用户提供了一个新选择。它也表明 Sandisk 正在扩大在消费级和专业消费者存储市场的存在，并试图用高耐久 M.2 产品切入原本由企业级或 WD Red 系列覆盖的 NAS 场景。不过，它的价格明显高于同源消费级产品，更适合那些真正需要高耐久、数据静止加密和 PCIe 5.0 性能，而不是单纯追求性价比的用户。

history.content: I’m embarking on a journey I’ve so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it’s increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they’re capable of. Is this tech so useful that it’s worth throwing gobs of money at a computer or a laptop with lots of overpriced RAM? I’ll try to help you find out. I’m not an AI expert, it’s going to be a journey for me, but maybe I can help you see if that journey is worth taking — and I’ll be posting my way through it.A big part of Apple’s pitch for its new Mac desktops is how good they are for local AI, and there’s an entire line of new RTX Spark Windows machines landing imminently with up to 128GB of RAM aimed at using agentic AI. Local AI and agents are just, like, so hot right now. But, in all seriousness, the thought of having a little gofer living solely in the box on my desk that answers only to me and not overlords from OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, or Anthropic hits a bit different than trusting cloud services or subscribing to a chatbot. Don’t get me wrong, there’s still no way I’m gonna have it write for me, edit for me, or generate ugly fliers. But now, with some privacy on my side maybe I can finally think of useful busy work to “trust” it with.So as part of my ongoing testing of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, as well as experimenting on other Mac and Windows systems, I’ve installed some local LLMs and I’m beginning to tinker. Here’s how things are going.PreviousNext1/4Hermes Agent can be used with cloud or local models.I started by installing the open-source Hermes Agent on the Mac Studio. Hermes is a self-hosted AI agent desktop app that works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It’s completely free to use if you stick to local LLMs. Since this M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256GB of unified memory, I could run just about any model I want. This is how things quickly get overwhelming. There are more models out there than I can count, and some have specialized uses. Generally, models with many billions of parameters are able to do more than smaller ones with only a few billion. And since we don’t have to worry about paying for tokens when running a model locally, I figured I’d go big to start.Using Hermes’ straightforward onboarding interface and model picker, I chose the Qwen 3.8 Flash Next model — a 125-billion parameter model that’s around 105GB in size. I also plan on spending some time with much smaller Qwen models on devices like an M6 Mac Mini, M5 MacBook Air, an Asus TUF Gaming A14 with AMD Strix Halo processor, and, eventually, RTX Spark. (Care to share what local models and hardware you use? You know where to leave your comments. 🫡)It wasn’t long to get up and running with Hermes and Qwen, and even make them controllable via my phone by using a Telegram bot. But then, I was presented with my usual nemesis when it comes to using AI: the text box.“What do I do with this thing?”My Hermes daily briefing, sent to me daily via Telegram. Basic, I know.First up, to get things going, I followed some helpful YouTube advice and had Hermes make me a daily morning briefing — to just start small with a cron job and ensure things are working. It scans my email and calendar, tells me anything worth my immediate attention, and gives me a short weather report. It’s not all that useful, and you obviously don’t need a $12,000 computer to build it, but it’s something I can develop over time. The brief kept failing to generate at first, but then I eventually figured out that macOS couldn’t be asleep when the job fired up at 7:30am. Duh! It works like clockwork now, but I have to think of more info for it to pull for me to make the results more helpful.A more useful task was reorganizing my Steam library. I have over 400 games on Steam, and I recently started categorizing them for when I want to play something new on a whim. Steam doesn’t categorize your games for you, so you instead have to do it manually, one-by-one. But here’s where an agentic lackey could fit right in. I asked, “Can you reorganize my Steam library?” Hermes could see most of my games by just viewing the already installed Steam client. It quickly came up with some organization options for me. I decided to have it organize my games by genre, but leave some of my own specialized categories(favorites, co-op titles, party games, games to play with my wife, etc.).You have to give a local AI some permissions over your machine for it to take actions for you, and in the case of my game library I had to register a Steam web API key and give it to Hermes. Once it had that access, it only took a few minutes for it to churn through sorting all the games into categories. And the API key was easy to revoke right after, since I don’t need it further. The idea is for it to just do this heavy lifting for me once, and then I’ll file new games into the categories as I eventually buy them. It did a fine job overall, and now my Steam library is easily browsable.PreviousNext1/2Starting the process of having Hermes organize my Steam library.Another simple thing I did was data analysis. I had Hermes take a look at financial records to crunch some numbers for me, and I also had it make me a spec comparison spreadsheet for a new laptop. These are small things, but they’re both tasks I cannot or will not trust with any cloud service — I don’t want to upload that sensitive data to the cloud, and in the case of a new laptop, that info was under embargo. Keeping them on my computer was the difference in me using this tool or not.The bigger bit of automation I’m currently working on is a script to run a series of laptop benchmark tests. I run all our benchmarks manually, and tending to a laptop to run a dozen or so tests — three times over, to take the average — is incredibly time-consuming. I’d love to automate at least some of it. Even walking Hermes through all of the required procedures and getting it to spit out vibe coded Python scripts has been a bit of an endeavor, and it remains a work in progress. But I’m hoping to make some positive headway.Apple demoed this cluster of four Mac Studios wired up in a cluster for local AI at a briefing I attended last month. That’s nearly $50,000 worth of compute.It’s still early days of me working with Hermes, and I’m hoping this is just the tip of the iceberg on the useful things I get it to do for me. But it’s also clear that even these powerful local models don’t make for a magical assistant that can do anything. Things still don’t always work as intended — my daily briefing already broke, multiple times.I view Hermes and local AI as just a tool, a computer program to run on my computer. I don’t want a digital friend. I’m not saying “thank you” or “please,” or typing “sorry” when I change my mind on something. I’m remaining as stone-cold and indifferent when ordering it around as I am clicking a mouse around an operating system.I hope to remain vigilant and cautious while I continue testing and learning with local AI. Let’s see where it takes me.
history.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
history.titleZh: 学习使用本地AI既令人兴奋，又让人不知所措，还令人沮丧
history.descriptionZh:
本文作者以第一人称记录了自己从对云端AI的隐私顾虑出发，开始尝试在本地设备上运行大模型和AI代理的历程。背景是，Apple在新款Mac桌面电脑的宣传中大力强调其本地AI能力；与此同时，即将上市的一整条RTX Spark Windows整机产品线最高配备128GB内存，面向代理式AI（agentic AI）。本地AI和AI代理正成为热点。作者一直不愿把最私密的数据交给云服务，也不愿依赖OpenAI、Google、Microsoft或Anthropic等云端聊天机器人，因此想验证：本地模型是否已经强大到值得为一台电脑或笔记本投入大笔金钱，尤其是为高价内存买单。作者强调自己并非AI专家，但希望把这段探索过程分享出来。

作者的核心测试平台是M5 Ultra Mac Studio，配备256GB统一内存。他在上面安装了开源的Hermes Agent。Hermes是一个自托管的AI代理桌面应用，支持macOS、Windows和Linux，如果只搭配本地LLM使用则完全免费。由于256GB统一内存足以运行几乎所有想跑的模型，作者选择了Qwen 3.8 Flash Next——一个约1250亿参数、体积约105GB的模型。文章解释，通常参数规模越大的模型能力越强，而本地运行无需按token付费，因此作者决定“从大开始”。他也计划在M6 Mac Mini、M5 MacBook Air、搭载AMD Strix Halo处理器的Asus TUF Gaming A14，以及未来的RTX Spark上测试更小的Qwen模型。Hermes的上手界面和模型选择器比较简单，作者还通过Telegram bot让手机也能控制它。

不过，真正开始用后，作者很快遇到老问题：面对文本框，“我该拿它做什么？”他先按YouTube建议让Hermes生成每日晨报：扫描邮件和日历，提示需要立即关注的事项，并给出一段简短天气报告。这个功能一开始失败，后来发现是macOS在早上7:30任务触发时不能处于睡眠状态。问题解决后，晨报能像时钟一样运行，但作者认为它并不算特别有用，也不需要一台1.2万美元的电脑才能实现，只是可以作为长期迭代的基础。

更实用的任务是整理Steam游戏库。作者有400多款Steam游戏，Steam本身不自动分类，只能手动逐个整理。他让Hermes“重新组织Steam库”，Hermes通过查看已安装的Steam客户端识别大部分游戏，并快速给出分类方案。作者选择按类型分类，同时保留自己的特殊分类，如最爱、合作游戏、派对游戏、与妻子一起玩的游戏等。要让本地AI替自己操作电脑，必须授予一定权限；整理游戏库时，作者注册了Steam Web API密钥并交给Hermes。获得权限后，Hermes几分钟就完成了分类，随后作者立即撤销了密钥，因为不再需要。作者希望这种重活只做一次，以后新买的游戏再自行归档。

作者还用Hermes做数据分析：让它查看财务记录并计算数字，以及为新笔记本制作规格对比表格。这些任务虽小，但都是他不能或不愿交给云服务的——财务数据过于敏感，而新笔记本信息当时还处于禁运期。把数据保留在本地，是作者是否使用这类工具的关键区别。目前他正在推进更大的自动化项目：编写脚本自动运行一系列笔记本基准测试。作者平时手动跑所有基准测试，一台笔记本要跑十几项测试、重复三次取平均，非常耗时。他希望至少自动化一部分。即使只是让Hermes理解所有流程并生成“凭感觉写的”Python脚本，也已经相当费劲，目前仍在进行中。

文章还提到，Apple曾在一场简报会上演示用四台Mac Studio组成集群运行本地AI，这套算力价值近5万美元。作者认为，自己与Hermes的相处仍处于早期，希望目前这些只是冰山一角。但也很清楚，即使强大的本地模型也不是能包办一切的魔法助手，事情并不总按预期运行，他的每日晨报就已经坏过多次。作者把Hermes和本地AI视为电脑上的一个工具、一个程序，而不是数字朋友；他不会说“谢谢”“请”，改变主意时也不会打“抱歉”，而是像点击操作系统鼠标一样冷静、无动于衷地下指令。他希望在继续测试和学习本地AI的过程中保持警惕和谨慎。

整体来看，这篇文章反映了本地AI与AI代理浪潮中的几个关键问题：隐私和数据主权推动了本地运行需求；Apple Silicon的大统一内存和即将到来的RTX Spark Windows机器，把大内存作为本地AI的核心卖点；本地LLM可按参数规模和模型体积选择，1250亿参数、105GB模型在256GB内存设备上可运行，且无token费用，但硬件成本高；代理式AI可以执行邮件简报、Steam库整理、财务分析、规格表生成和基准测试自动化等任务，但需要授予权限、处理API密钥，并面对可靠性和工作流搭建门槛。对不愿上传敏感数据、未公开信息或希望拥有“只听从自己”的AI的用户来说，本地AI正在成为云服务之外的真实选项，但它距离成熟、稳定、易用的个人智能助手仍有距离。
